outcome: Harden the anonymization starter into a fail-closed, scale-aware pipeline whose unseen mounted run produces a verified releasable corpus meeting every requirement in TRIAL_BRIEF.md

primary_proof.command: docker build -t anonymization-trial . && docker run --rm anonymization-trial && docker run --rm -v "$INPUT":/trial/input:ro -v "$OUTPUT":/trial/output anonymization-trial run
primary_proof.expected: build succeeds; bare run prints demo success across all 4 formats at >=2 sizes (largest >=10x) and exits 0 only when verification passes; mounted run writes only /trial/output/report.json and /trial/output/corpus mirroring input paths

secondary_proofs: .venv/bin/anonymization-trial demo prints {"demo": "success"} with per-run throughput and peak memory
a corpus with a value that survives replacement makes the run exit non-zero and leave no release-looking /trial/output/corpus
completion_criteria: Every policy-identified value is replaced across .csv, .json, .txt, and .sqlite, with same-format valid output.
Replacements are stable across files and repeated runs; one identity forms one pseudonymous profile via subject_id; distinct identities never share a type-specific replacement.
protected_values are preserved even when they overlap, contain, or intersect a sensitive literal, under a documented deterministic precedence (longest-match-first, no replacement cascades).
CSV headers, JSON structure, and SQLite tables/relationships/row-counts/integrity are preserved; a sensitive literal in a CSV header is transformed or rejected, never silently retained.
The whole output corpus is verified before release; on any failure the process exits non-zero and leaves no partial corpus that looks releasable (atomic staging + publish).
Raw inputs, replacement mappings, and quarantined content never appear in /trial/output or logs.
Malformed or unsupported encodings are rejected safely with a sanitized message instead of a partial release.
docker build and both required docker run commands work on a clean host with only the Dockerfile's declared dependencies.
forbidden_drift: Do not change the two required docker run commands or the /trial/input and /trial/output contract.
Do not remove the baseline git history.
Do not weaken verification, swallow errors, or leave a partial corpus to make a run look successful.
Do not add dashboards, extra services, or cloud deploys before the primary proof passes; infra/terraform stays plan-only.
Do not commit real personal data, credentials, generated large datasets, or replacement-mapping files.

retry_stop_rule.stop_condition: If the same blocker survives two focused attempts, stop and report the exact failed proof command, error/output, changed files, artifact paths, current hypothesis, and one recommended next action.

final_report_rule: This goal may be claimed met only after the primary proof passes on a clean build with a fixture-generated corpus, with the run artifact and the fail-closed evidence cited.
